Ring and Glance

Ring is the logo: a heavy o with an orange point, and if you look long enough it reads o8. Glance is the pet that lives inside the product. Glance is now fog everywhere: its body fades into whatever it sits on, while the eyes and orange dot stay sharp. That includes the small sizes and every locked motion.

Each state on its own

How it maps: taking in work is Many in, one out. Reviewing is Read the diff. Sending back turns Glance orange and sends the findings out. Waiting on CI is Fan out, the three lanes being the checks. Re-reviewing is Branch review. Merging is Glance to Merge. Approved is the seal, at the end. Thinking is the resting loop in between. Each state keeps its motion’s edge rule, so the indicator moves between fog and hard edges with the work. In the composer it uses tight fog at 40px.

Glance in fogLocked

No hard body. The pebble becomes fog: solid in the middle, fading evenly outward into nothing, so Glance sits in any surface instead of on top of it. The eyes and the orange dot stay crisp, because that’s where the character is. Ring and everything else stays flat.

On any surface

States in fog

The locked color states carry over: the fog takes the state color.

Small sizes

Full fog smudges below 48px (the ✗ ones), so the fade shrinks with the size. Tight from 24 to 40px keeps a visible soft edge of a pixel or two. Hairline at 16 and 20px is the honest limit: the face reads fine, but the fade is under a pixel, so it looks nearly flat. The app icon and favicon stay Ring.

Motion

The rule: Fog at 48px and up, tight from 24 to 40px, hairline at 16 and 20px, never below 16px. Motions follow the edge rules in the Motion section. Ring, the app icon and the favicon stay flat. Mist is for big backdrops only.

Intro: Wake

Ring holds, crisp and flat, then softens into fog Glance while it’s still half asleep, and the orange point drops last. It goes back to a flat Ring at the end, so the logo itself is never fogged.

A story to hold it together

What Sofiane’s post does well, and a saga built on what o8 actually does.

What Sishen Security does

“A security startup built on the four guardians of Chinese mythology. One beast watches each side of your company.”

  • One sentence holds the world. You get the whole brand from the caption.
  • The myth maps to the product. Each beast owns one area of security, so the story is also the feature list.
  • Detail in the art, restraint in the type. Chrome-rendered guardians next to a plain mono font; a reply calls that pairing out.

I could read the captions and replies, but not the images or video, so this is from the words only.

What o8 can borrow

  • One sentence: every change gets a second pair of eyes.
  • A canon that maps 1:1: each part of the story is one real thing o8 does, never two.
  • Restraint: their art is detailed; ours stays flat. What carries over is the story, not the chrome.

The saga is the loop Locked

No made-up names. o8’s story is the six steps it already takes with every change, from the README and roadmap on main today. Each step has its own spot for the Ring’s point, starting at the logo’s home. The era is whichever step o8 is making real right now, and the loop closing is 1.0.

Today: the Re-review era. Small orange dots are steps that work on main, the big point is the one being built, and the paper dots are still ahead.

How it shows up

In the app

The same six words are the status of every piece of work in the sidebar, and Glance wears the matching face. Settings → About shows the Ring with the current step’s point.

On the site

One strip of six steps under the hero. Steps that work today are solid, the one being built has the orange point, the rest are outlines. It updates when a step ships.

In release posts

Every post leads with its step: “o8 0.1.82x · Re-review. Fixes now get checked against the saved findings.” The clip is the locked motion for that step.

The rule that keeps us in line: every release names the step it moves forward, and only claims a step once it works on main. If work doesn’t move one of the six, it waits. Logo and Glance stay flat.

Motion studies

Glance acting out what o8 does. Edges follow your rule: Fan out, Read the diff and Branch review are hard edged. Approve is fog while it’s Glance and goes hard as it becomes the seal with the check. Many in, one out is fog on the in side and sharp on the out side. The ones you called fire are locked; the rest are still up for grabs.

Rules so far

  • Two marks, two jobs: Ring stands for the app and stays flat; Glance stands for the agent and is fog. Never put both side by side as a lockup.
  • Colors: ink and paper, one orange point. Glance only turns orange to say “sent back”.
  • Fog: Glance’s body is always fog. Full fog at 48px and up, tight from 24 to 40px, hairline at 16 and 20px, never below 16px. Eyes and the orange dot stay crisp.
  • Character: eyes look right by default. No brows, arms, hats or extra faces. Detail gets added slowly, if at all.
  • Motion: every loop starts and ends on Glance, eases in and out, and pauses when the system asks for reduced motion.
